chapter: Life in New York in the 1940s
title: New York musicians' bars and whiskey drinkers
summary: Edison recalls bars like Jim and Andy's, the Turf and Beefsteak Charlie's, where whiskey drinkers outlasted heroin users.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, you know, there again, you see if the guy is a kind of alcoholic and then he puts a big meal down, then he probably is going to feel better.

Oh, yeah, he'll feel better. There's no doubt. If you can get the meal down, you know. But it seems like most of the older generation, they drank whiskey, you know. Like we were talking about the places in New York, yesterday,

when we were coming from a blues memorial service yesterday, about the New York places you used to meet all the musicians, Jim & Andy's , the Turf, the Copper: /, the other one that you were mentioning where Paul Webster and Hilton --
Beefsteak Charlie's, you know. Those guys drank whiskey, you know. Had they gone for heroin, they wouldn't have lasted that long. They wouldn't have lasted that long.
People like Johnny Hodges even gave up pot.
Well, they usually give it up. Well, it's the -- I think nowadays the musicians, they reach greater heights too quick. They don't know how to handle it, you know. Than we did.
